subproblem.title: Cut-off of the pulled-back form: a continuous compactly supported covector field equal to ω(f(x))∘Df(x) on K
subproblem.statement: Let P, Q, n ∈ ℕ, O ⊆ ℝ^P open, K ⊆ O compact, f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q of class C¹ on O (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O), and ω : ℝ^Q → Λⁿ(ℝ^Q) a continuous n-form (DifferentialForm (Euclid Q) n). Then there is a continuous, compactly supported covector field h : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P) (Covector (Euclid P) n) with h(x) = ω(f(x))∘Df(x) := (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x) for every x ∈ K.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q n : ℕ) (O K : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → Euclid Q) (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid Q) n), IsOpen O → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O → IsCompact K → K ⊆ O → Continuous ω → ∃ h : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n, Continuous h ∧ HasCompactSupport h ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, h x = (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–2 of the parent proof. This is the cut-off ζ of Simon Ch. 6, 2.23 (chapter-06.txt lines 408–412: ζ ∈ C_c^∞(U) identically one in a neighbourhood of the compact set spt T ∩ spt f^#ω), applied to the pulled-back form x ↦ ω(f(x))∘Df(x) of 2.24(2) (lines 415–424), which makes sense for f merely C¹. Two harmless generalizations of the parent's setting: the target space is ℝ^Q (the parent uses Q = P), and ω is any continuous n-form on ℝ^Q (the parent's test form is C^∞, hence continuous). Only continuity of the cut-off is used.
Notation: Λⁿ(V) := Covector V n, the continuous alternating n-linear maps Vⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm. Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x ∈ L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q). γ(x) := ω(f(x))∘Df(x) := (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x) ∈ Λⁿ(ℝ^P), so γ(x)(v₁, …, vₙ) = ω(f(x))(Df(x)v₁, …, Df(x)vₙ). thickening(r, K) := {x : infEdist(x, K) < r} is open; cthickening(r, K) := {x : infEdist(x, K) ≤ r} is closed.
1. f and Df are continuous on O. Since f is C¹ on O, f is continuous on O (ContDiffOn.continuousOn). Since O is open and 1 ≤ 1, Df = fderiv ℝ f is continuous on O (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen hf hO le_rfl).
2. The pull-back map is continuous. Let Φ : Λⁿ(ℝ^Q) × L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q) → Λⁿ(ℝ^P), Φ(β, A) := β.compContinuousLinearMap A. Mathlib shows Φ has a strict Fréchet derivative at every point (ContinuousAlternatingMap.hasStrictFDerivAt_compContinuousLinearMap), and such a map is continuous at that point (HasStrictFDerivAt.continuousAt). So Φ is continuous (continuous_iff_continuousAt). Equivalently, Φ(β, A) = compContinuousLinearMapCLM A β, where A ↦ compContinuousLinearMapCLM A is continuous (ContinuousAlternatingMap.continuous_compContinuousLinearMapCLM) and evaluation is jointly continuous; in coordinates Φ is a polynomial in the entries of β and A.
3. γ is continuous on O. x ↦ ω(f(x)) is continuous on O, since ω is continuous and f is continuous on O (Continuous.comp_continuousOn). With step 1, x ↦ (ω(f(x)), Df(x)) is continuous on O (ContinuousOn.prodMk). So γ = Φ ∘ (x ↦ (ω(f(x)), Df(x))) is continuous on O by step 2.
4. Margin. K is compact, O is open and K ⊆ O, so there is ρ > 0 with cthickening(ρ, K) ⊆ O (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open); write ρ = 2δ. The set cthickening(ρ, K) is compact, because K is compact and ℝ^P is proper (IsCompact.cthickening).
5. Cut-off. Let s := thickening(ρ, K), which is open, and t := cthickening(ρ/2, K), which is closed. Since 0 < ρ/2 < ρ, t ⊆ s (cthickening_subset_thickening'). Apply the smooth Urysohn lemma in the finite-dimensional space ℝ^P (exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff) to the open s and the closed t ⊆ s, with any smoothness order, e.g. 0. This gives χ : ℝ^P → ℝ with values in [0, 1], continuous (ContDiff.continuous), support χ = s, and χ(x) = 1 for every x ∈ t. A continuous Urysohn function, e.g. from exists_tsupport_one_of_isOpen_isClosed, would serve equally well. Then:
 (a) χ(x) = 1 for every x ∈ K, because K ⊆ t (self_subset_cthickening);
 (b) tsupport χ = closure(s) ⊆ cthickening(ρ, K) (closure_thickening_subset_cthickening). Hence tsupport χ ⊆ O by step 4, and tsupport χ lies in the compact set cthickening(ρ, K).
6. Definition. For every x ∈ ℝ^P put h(x) := χ(x)·γ(x) ∈ Λⁿ(ℝ^P), using scalar multiplication in Λⁿ(ℝ^P). γ(x) is defined for every x through fderiv, but is controlled only on O.
7. h has compact support. If χ(x) = 0 then h(x) = 0, so tsupport h ⊆ tsupport χ (tsupport_smul_subset_left). tsupport h is closed and contained in the compact set cthickening(ρ, K) (step 5(b)), so it is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset). That is, HasCompactSupport h.
8. h is continuous. On O, h is the product of the continuous real function χ and the function γ, which is continuous on O by step 3; so h is continuous on O (ContinuousOn.smul). Also tsupport h ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ O by steps 5(b) and 7. A function that is continuous on an open set containing its topological support is continuous everywhere (ContinuousOn.continuous_of_tsupport_subset): at points of O use continuity on the open set O, and at points outside tsupport h, h vanishes on the open neighbourhood ℝ^P ∖ tsupport h. So h is continuous.
9. h agrees with γ on K. For x ∈ K, χ(x) = 1 by step 5(a), so h(x) = 1·γ(x) = (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x).
10. By steps 7–9, h is continuous, has compact support, and satisfies h(x) = (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x) for every x ∈ K, as claimed. ∎
proof_key_steps: f and Df are continuous on the open set O (f is C¹), and (β, A) ↦ β∘A is jointly continuous (strict derivative), so γ = ω(f)∘Df is continuous on O.
Margin cthickening(ρ, K) ⊆ O, and a Urysohn cut-off χ with χ = 1 on K and compact tsupport χ ⊆ cthickening(ρ, K) ⊆ O.
h := χ·γ satisfies tsupport h ⊆ tsupport χ, so h has compact support; h is continuous on the open set O ⊇ tsupport h, hence continuous; h = γ on K.

audit.reason: The prose includes every hypothesis and matches the exact Lean proposition. C¹ regularity on open O gives continuity of f and its ambient derivative; joint continuity of alternating-map composition gives the pullback's continuity. The compact thickening and Urysohn cutoff establish compact support, global continuity, and agreement on K. The generalization to P → Q and continuous ω is justified, with no circular dependency.
